questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to choose a city where I could feel safe and comfortable, while also offering many opportunities. I was already familiar with the city and the language, which was a plus for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I have been very happy with my stay at FU Berlin.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The amount of information has generally been sufficient. However, there have been many emails to keep track of before, during, and after the exchange program.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a couple of very informative orientation days and the Erasmus Team at FU has been very good and quick in responding to my emails whenever I had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My experience was that it is really difficult to find housing i Berlin. I had some contacts who helped me a lot.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That they should not feel pressured about their housing situation too early. My impression is that the housing market in Berlin moves very quickly, and that it is common for people to start looking for new tenants only a month in advance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, the orientation days were very informative. So everything after was pretty intuitive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration is done through Campus Management. From there, I could find the courses that I found interesting in the course catalog. It was very easy. It was also possible to prioritize the seminars. I needed to have three lectures with three corresponding seminars to get the 30 ECTS.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was always possible for me to send an email to the Erasmus Team at FU who responded quickly to my emails. Otherwise, I would ask someone from my lectures.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is an extended period during which you can register and de-register for various seminars. This can also be done after the semester and the classes have started if you find that your chosen seminars are not as interesting as you expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I don't understand the question. I think the level of courses was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more discussion-oriented. It was also common to have to present a text or subject, moderate the class, and complete weekly assignments in the seminars throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Globalization and Regional Development
- Nation-State, Citizenship, and Globalization
- LECTURE Cultural Differences and Similarities between the Member States of the European Union
- Religiosity in European Societies
- LECTURE Social Structure of European Societies
- Immigrant integration in Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Nation-State, Citizenship, and Globalization, LECTURE Social Structure of European Societies, and Immigrant integration in Europe

questions.answer: It was less expensive to go out or buy groceries than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different social activities like football.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any of the athletic activities at my host institution but I know that other students are happy with the social activities there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The city of Berlin is very big and it has a bit of everything. There is a lot of different bars, clubs, museums, events and parks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My impression was that everyone is very kind and welcoming. So, just be open to meeting new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences that were challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone I met was very kind, open and curious. I don't know if that is a cultural thing, but I appreciated it a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The variety of course options
2. The number of activities you can do on weekends and holidays
3. The diversity within the city

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you normally live in Copenhagen, it takes some adjustment to live in a larger city such as Berlin. Freie Universität is located a bit further out from Berlin, so you need to get used to the commute. That was the hardest part for me. It was an hour of transportation each way, whereas I am used to a 15-minute bike ride. But after some weeks you get used to it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all the great people - both from Erasmus and from my study department.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my friends and family in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
